messages:
alex: FYI opened escal for ACME complaining embedding throughput dropped ~3x overnight. they say embeddings.v1 requests still succeed but throughput (vectors/sec) down. tokens/sec for their text gen routes looks normal.

maria: ugh. any error codes in their traces? latency or 429s?

alex: no 5xx/4xx at API layer. just queueing. their reported numbers: was ~120k vectors/sec, now ~40-50k. spikes at request bursts.

jordan: first thought: batching fallback? if dimension mismatch or smaller dims might disable some batch kernels. alex can you share a repro?

alex: pasted repro they sent. small python loop calling /v1/embeddings with batch_size=128, input length ~100 tokens each. they also send an earlier curl: 

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embedding-xl-1536","input":["a","b",...128 items]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

lisa: model is embedding-xl-1536, right? customer mentioned recently switching from embedding-l-768 -> xl-1536 yesterday. could be quantization/kernel mismatch.

maria: check runtime logs for batcher decisions and kernel selection. sometimes a kernel update can drop vectorized path for 1536 dims.

jordan: pinging eng-runtime. @sre-bot can we get GPU util + queue depth for nodes serving embeddings-xl-1536 in region us-east-1 between 03:00-06:00 UTC?

sre-bot: collecting metrics... will post soon.

(sre-bot later) sre-bot: metrics snapshot attached:

```
# top aggregated across node pool (03:30 UTC)
GPU util: 92-95%
Memory used: 78%
Compute SM avg: 91%
Average batch size: 8-12 (requests per batch)
Queue depth: high, avg wait 120ms -> 450ms during bursts
vectors/sec (per node): dropped from 60k -> 18k
```

maria: interesting — GPU saturated but batch sizes are tiny (8-12). previously we saw batch size ~48-96 which drove vectors/sec up. something causing batcher to flush early.

alex: customer logs show occasional warning: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768" but only for a tiny subset of calls. could those mismatches be causing fallback to single-request path?

jordan: yes. if the serving runtime sees mixed dims in a batch it may break batching or route to compatibility kernel (slow). need to confirm whether mixed dims present in same worker queue.

lisa: also check client side — are they sending a mix of models in same endpoint? earlier we allowed multi-model routing but if client sometimes posts model:embedding-l-768 and sometimes xl-1536 to same endpoint it can cause small batches.

alex: customer says they started A/B testing new model but forgot to separate endpoints. they had two periodic jobs hitting same endpoint with different dims.

maria: that would explain high GPU util + small batch sizes + dimension mismatch warnings. solution: quarantine models or reject mixed-dim batches. but need to be careful — we typically auto-fallback, which might be slower.

jordan: immediate mitigation: add server-side guard to reject mixed-dimension microbatches with clear 400 error so customers see explicit failure instead of silent slow path. can we patch canary? @deploy-bot schedule?

deploy-bot: canary rollout queued (canary group: 5%) if eng-runtime approves. requested by @jordan.

alex: repro steps I used locally to simulate:
1) spawn two processes hitting same embeddings endpoint, one sends 128x 768 vectors, other sends 128x 1536 vectors concurrently.
2) watch batch sizes in runtime logs and nvidia-smi.

python snippet they used:
```python
import requests, threading

def worker(model, n=128):
    payload = {"model": model, "input": ["text"]*n}
    r = requests.post(API, json=payload, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {TOKEN}"})
    print(r.status_code, len(r.json().get('data',[])))

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(m,)) for m in ("embedding-l-768","embedding-xl-1536")]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```

lisa: good repro. ok next steps:
- short term: server will start returning 400 for mixed-dim batch submissions in 1hr canary. (owner: jordan)
- mid term: enhance batcher to keep dimension-partitioned queues so mixed dims don't reduce batch sizes. (owner: eng-runtime)
- notify customer: explain root cause + workaround (owner: alex)

maria: also performance regression note: the vectors/sec metric dropped primarily because the batcher fell back to per-request kernel for mixed dims; tokens/sec unaffected because generation pipeline separate. record this in incident.

ajira: (support-bot) created ticket INC-2026-4523 and attached logs.

alex: emailed customer with workaround: use separate endpoints or ensure consistent model dims in same workload. they ack'd, but want platform fix.

jordan: can we add telemetry alert that flags high GPU util + avg batch size < X for embeddings pool? that would catch regressions earlier.

lisa: yes. filed ENGOPS-987. set alert: gpu_util > 85% && avg_batch_size < 16 for 5m.

maria: note for postmortem: check deploy history — did we push any kernel or kernel selector changes around 03:00 UTC? if so that may have amplified the regression but root cause is mixed dims.

sre-bot: deploy history shows a runtime config tweak at 02:45 UTC rolling 10% to canary: "batcher: kernel_selector: prefer_vector_kernels_v2". rollback not yet triggered.

jordan: let's hold canary until we add dim-based partitioning or clear reject behavior. I'll pause the rollout.

(30m later) jordan: patched canary to return explicit 400 when mixed-dim batches detected. rolling 5% now. logs show dimension-mismatch metric spikes then drop as customers fix clients.

alex: customer confirmed vectors/sec recovered after separating jobs into distinct endpoints. they want timeline for permanent fix.

lisa: plan for permanent: 1) dim-partitioned queues + kernel selector improvements, 2) better telemetry + customer-facing error when models mixed, 3) docs update + quickstart note about model dims for embeddings.

maria: final action items:
- jordan: own canary guard + follow up on kernel-selector (in progress)
- eng-runtime: design doc for dim-partitioned batching (ETA 2 weeks)
- alex: customer comms + close support ticket once patch in prod
- lisa: alerts + postmortem writeup (include graphs tokens/sec vs vectors/sec)

alex: thanks all. assigning follow-ups in the ticket. :thumbsup:
